text.p: President Clinton on Saturday honoured Chicago's Cardinal Joseph Bernardin, who died of pancreatic cancer on Thursday, as a great American who devoted himself to bringing out the best in humanity.

"He taught us that what unites us is more important than what divides us, that we can meet our challenges, but only by coming together across our differences," Clinton said in his weekly radio address.

"As he said shortly before he died, 'It is wrong to waste the precious gift of time given to us on acrimony and division,'" the president said, urging all Americans to strive to find the common ground Bernardin fought so hard to achieve.
Clinton said Americans had seen the high price of discrimination and hatred.
"But we also know how much is possible when people find unity and strength in their diversity," he said.

"This week, we lost a great American who taught us the importance of this lesson, and whom people all over the world looked up to as the embodiment of the values that keep America strong: Cardinal Joseph Bernardin of Chicago," Clinton said.
"As one of the most influential Roman Catholics in modern history, Cardinal Bernardin devoted himself to bringing out the best in humanity."

Bernardin died of pancreatic cancer after a highly public battle with the disease during which he kept a busy schedule until a few days before the death that he said he welcomed as a gift and a "transition from earthly life to life eternal."
Clinton said he and Hillary Rodham Clinton counted Bernardin as their friend and would miss him very much.
